correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the exact source recurrence gives the unique positive primitive two-cycle for r>r1. A two-step -1 Floquet eigenvector is exactly a four-phase anti-periodic sequence, reducing the original M-dimensional eigencondition to a 2x2 determinant. Its determinant is K-(r-1+t)(r-r1), strictly decreasing for r>r1, giving one and only one resonance. The strict K>0 follows from positivity of the imaginary component; tails of signed GL weights at -1 and -i are O(M^-1-q), while the constant-mode tail is M^-q/Gamma(1-q). Taylor expansion gives the positive coefficient. A standalone standard-library checker directly evaluates the original recurrence and four-phase equation at 24 order-memory pairs and the asymptotic coefficient at nine pairs. These finite checks are not proofs of the universal statements.

value.rationale: The source explicitly motivates quantitative large-memory shifts of the period-doubling cascade but computes the period-two boundary implicitly and extrapolates higher-level thresholds. An explicit all-memory second resonance and its exact M^-q coefficient permit analytic comparison of truncation errors and expose noncommuting zero-order/infinite-memory limits. These are structurally motivated quantitative properties of the next natural cascade level, not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite-table recomputation. No unsupported full-memory periodicity or generic period-four bifurcation is claimed.
